<span id="h2-auto-generated-key-backfill" />

# Auto-generated Key Backfill

H2 supports common `IDENTITY` auto-increment columns and also sequences. Under H2, dbVisitor primarily uses JDBC generated keys or pre-insert sequence reading to handle primary keys.

## IDENTITY Column

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_info (
    id   BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(64),
    age  INT
)
```

## Lambda / BaseMapper

Entity mapping uses `KeyType.Auto`:

```java title='H2 IDENTITY mapping'
@Table("user_info")
public class UserInfo {
    @Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Auto)
    private Long id;

    @Column("name")
    private String name;

    @Column("age")
    private Integer age;
}
```

```java title='Read backfilled primary key after Lambda insert'
UserInfo user = new UserInfo();
user.setName("mali");
user.setAge(18);

LambdaTemplate lambda = ...
lambda.insert(UserInfo.class)
      .applyEntity(user)
      .executeSumResult();

Long id = user.getId();
```

The H2 dialect can use regular JDBC batch when no backfill columns exist; once generated key backfill is required, it falls back to row-by-row execution to ensure stable backfill for each row.

## Mapper XML

```xml title='H2 generated keys'
<insert id="insertUser"
        useGeneratedKeys="true"
        keyProperty="id"
        keyColumn="id">
    INSERT INTO user_info (name, age)
    VALUES (#{name}, #{age})
</insert>
```

## Annotation Mapper

```java
@Insert(
    value = "INSERT INTO user_info (name, age) VALUES (#{name}, #{age})",
    useGeneratedKeys = true,
    keyProperty = "id",
    keyColumn = "id"
)
int insertUser(UserInfo user);
```

## Sequence

H2 dialect supports reading sequences:

```sql
values next value for user_info_seq
```

Mapper XML can use `selectKey`:

```xml
<insert id="insertUser">
    <selectKey keyProperty="id" keyColumn="id" order="BEFORE">
        values next value for user_info_seq
    </selectKey>
    INSERT INTO user_info (id, name, age)
    VALUES (#{id}, #{name}, #{age})
</insert>
```

Lambda / BaseMapper can use `KeyType.Sequence`:

```java
@KeySeq("user_info_seq")
@Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Sequence)
private Long id;
```

## Dialect Strategy

H2's current strategy is as follows:

| Scenario | GeneratedKeyStrategy |
| --- | --- |
| No backfill columns | `JdbcBatch` |
| `Into` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Ignore` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Update` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |

`DuplicateKeyStrategy.Ignore` / `Update` are implemented via H2 `MERGE`, requiring primary key columns.

## Design Principles

- `IDENTITY`: use `KeyType.Auto` or `useGeneratedKeys=true`.
- sequence: use `selectKey` / `@SelectKeySql` / `KeyType.Sequence` to get value before INSERT.
- Batch inserts without backfill use JDBC batch; when backfill is needed, conservative row-by-row execution.
- General documentation: see [Generated Keys](../../guides/core/mapper/annotation_insert#generated-keys).
